‘Like a Disney movie’: Three wild dog brothers make Africa’s longest journey
events.summary:
As three siblings came of age and had to leave their pack, scientists tracked the dogs’ perilous 2,500-mile odyssey to find their own territory

It sounds like a Disney movie: three wild dogs, all brothers, on an epic journey to find a home of their own after their family tells them to leave. They dodge cars and hunters in search of a new life, navigating bushmeat snares and the hostility of a human-dominated landscape until they find a new haven on the African savannah.

But this is exactly what happened in Zambia last year, when three endangered African wild dogs made the longest-ever recorded single journey of any mammal from the continent. The brothers travelled more than 2,500 miles (4,100km) over eight months in their “dispersal” – when a young dog comes of age and must establish new territory to find a mate and start a family of their own.

events.summary:
Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile

Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.

Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

events.summary:
Noura Erakat says a Florida mayor shortened speaking time and banned discussion of investment in Israeli bonds

The human rights lawyer Noura Erakat was arrested on Tuesday at a Palm Beach county, Florida, budget hearing about the county’s more than $1bn investments in Israeli bonds.

Erakat, a prominent Palestinian American activist, legal scholar and Guardian contributor, was one of several people in attendance at the public commission hearing who were forcibly removed by local law enforcement. events.summary:
Mohammad Sharifullah, 28, was convicted of aiding the terrorist group that took credit for the suicide bombing

An Islamic State group member was sentenced on Wednesday to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 US service members and about 160 Afghans at the Kabul airport five years ago during the US military’s chaotic withdrawal from the country.

A federal jury in Virginia had convicted Mohammad Sharifullah in April of providing material support to the IS affiliate known as Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). But jurors could not agree whether he bore some responsibility for the airport bombing on 26 August 2021.

events.summary:
Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August

Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found.

Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse, which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning.

The sons of Imran Khan have accused Pakistan’s powerful army chief of a “personal vendetta” against the incarcerated former prime minister and expressed fears their father is being “slowly killed” in jail, as international pressure mounts over his prison conditions.

Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.

events.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes

events.summary: As Gamescom 2026 opens in Cologne, AI, hardware costs and slowing user growth are putting pressure on the global games industry despite its current strength.

events.title: Remembering Dolly Parton: 8 facts about the icon
events.summary: Dolly Parton, one of the world's most successful artists, has died at the age of 80. Here are some important and extraordinary facts about the country music superstar.

events.title: US country music legend Dolly Parton dies aged 80
events.summary: Representatives of the country music legend told US media that Dolly Parton died after a "brief battle with cancer." Parton's career spans more than half a century and includes a wide array of smash hits.

events.summary: After three seasons in the second division, Schalke are back in the Bundesliga. Just a year ago, few would have guessed that their revival would largely be 'Made in Bosnia.'

events.summary: The US is expanding sanctions on Iran's financial networks, targeting crypto, gold, aviation and shipping. DW spoke with analysts about what could change.

events.summary: Record-breaking heat and drought are putting urban trees at risk. Experts explain how to protect these essential assets and build city forests that can withstand the climate challenges ahead.

events.title: The new Bundesliga season is here, but has the glow gone?
events.summary: Another Bundesliga season arrives, but are the golden years of Germany's top football league already over, and what can it do to change its course?

events.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
events.summary: "Immune hubs" that actively defend the brain have been discovered in mouse skull marrow. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

events.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
events.summary: A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost six times the monthly minimum wage. As drug prices soar and medicine is in short supply, doctors say more patients are delaying or abandoning treatment.

events.title: Sydney Marathon medal wrongly shows German landmark
events.summary: A medal minted for finishers in the Sydney Marathon features a skyline of the city — with one landmark from rather far away. Organizers say the muddle only makes the medal "a little more unique."

events.title: Why Germany's gas storage levels are so low
events.summary: Germany's gas storage facilities are only 50% full as traders bet that wholesale prices will fall if the Iran war ends. With around three months until winter, DW asks whether the country can refill its reserves in time.

events.title: How Europe can better protect against extreme wildfires
events.summary: In another summer of European wildfires that have even seen wetlands burning, scientists say the situation is set to worsen in the future. What's needed is fire prevention and climate protection.

events.title: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prison
events.summary: A Chinese court ordered the former billionaire's assets to be confiscated and fined Evergrande-related companies billions of dollars.

events.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
events.summary: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

events.title: Food security under pressure from conflicts, extreme weather
events.summary:
Extreme weather and violent conflicts are threatening food production and trade across the globe. Experts are forecasting a super El Niño, which could further disrupt planting and harvests – and push millions more people into acute food insecurity. Meanwhile the ongoing wars with Iran and Ukraine are disrupting shipping and supply chains. 
 
Shawn Arita, Associate Research Professor at North Dakota State University, believes that transport problems outweigh supply concerns. "The food does exist, the availability does exist. The main issue currently speaking is that the movement is broken."

events.title: Climate change: Glacier loss and dry rivers threaten water security
events.summary: The world's rivers experienced one of their driest years in more than three decades in 2025, while glaciers continued to retreat and freshwater reserves kept declining, according to the World Meteorological Organization. The agency warns that climate change and growing water use are making the global water cycle more erratic, increasing the risk of both droughts and floods.

events.title: 'Sanctions won’t prevent us from doing our job' says ICC Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang
events.summary: In this edition of Perspective, the acting Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court tells FRANCE 24 that the court is needed now more than ever to ensure there is no gap for impunity. Mame Mandiaye Niang says the court’s job is to step in if domestic justice systems fail. The Senegalese judge is at the centre of a storm amid sanctions put on the court by the US after its issuing of arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant over Israel’s actions in Gaza. He explained how the sanctions affect his daily life but says it won’t stop the court doing its job.

events.title: Nicolas Winding Refn on nearly dying, reuniting with Ryan Gosling and why 'polarisation is success'
events.summary: Ten years after The Neon Demon, Nicolas Winding Refn is back with 'Her Private Hell', a neon-soaked fever dream starring Sophie Thatcher and Charles Melton. Speaking to FRANCE 24’s Eve Jackson at the Deauville American Film Festival, the Danish provocateur behind 'Drive' and 'Bronson' opens up about the near-death experience that changed his life, why he believes “polarisation is success” and his plans to make a third film with Ryan Gosling – 15 years after 'Drive'.

events.title: Gaza documentary 'NAZA' sparks political storm, threats against directors in Israel
events.summary: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" featuring anonymous military sources speaking about Israel's mass killing of civilians in Gaza has sparked a political firestorm in Israel. The film's directors and their families have received a wave of threats, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a plan for a bill aimed at revoking the citizenship of people who "defame IDF soldiers".

events.title: Spain: Images of floods after torrential rain
events.summary: At least one person was killed after torrential rain lashed eastern Spain overnight Wednesday, submerging streets and flooding buildings and metro stations.

events.title: English village holds symbolic vote to leave UK
events.summary: A village in Oxfordshire has held a symbolic referendum to leave the United Kingdom in protest against government plans to house up to 1,200 asylum seekers at a nearby military base. While the vote has no legal force, it highlights wider tensions over the UK's asylum policy and migration debate.

events.title: Mbappé draws fire from right wing in France, Spain over Ceuta t-shirt controversy
events.summary: Real Madrid's French forward Kylian Mbappé is facing mounting criticism by Spanish and French conservative and far-right politicians for partially obscuring a t-shirt supporting residents of Ceuta, Spain's territory bordering Morocco grappling with a migration crisis. Mbappé said he wore the t-shirt rolled up to show solidarity with "all the immigrants who have lost their lives".

events.title: Amnesty accuses Iran of crimes against humanity
events.summary: Amnesty International has accused Iranian authorities of committing crimes against humanity during the 2022 Woman, Life, Freedom crackdown, saying more than 500 people, including 71 children, were killed and that the violence disproportionately targeted Kurdish and Baluchi communities. The rights group is urging the UN General Assembly to create an international justice mechanism, arguing that many of the officials it identified remain in positions of power.

events.title: Houthis claim Saudi F-15 kill as Yemen fighting escalates
events.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels have released footage they say shows the wreckage of a Saudi F-15 fighter jet, which, if confirmed, would mark the first fighter jet they have shot down. The claim comes as fighting escalates in Yemen, with the Houthis expanding their control around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait and the UN urging both sides to return to negotiations.

events.title: Carney pushes Canada-EU ties beyond trade
events.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney used his address to the European Parliament to signal that Ottawa wants to deepen its partnership with the EU beyond trade, expanding cooperation on energy, AI, space and payment sovereignty, while also seeking to join the Erasmus programme. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating explains how the push reflects Canada's broader strategy to build stronger alliances beyond the United States without seeking to join the EU's single market, even as questions remain over how those ambitions can be turned into concrete action.

events.title: 'We must 'force' social media to redesign harmful algorithms, platforms that fuel addictive behavior
events.summary: Charles Pellegrin is pleased to welcome Hannah Storey, Head of Children and Young People’s Digital Rights at Amnesty International. Digital spaces can provide even young people with community, self-expression, education and opportunities for activism. The deeper problem, she warns, lies in the architecture of the platforms themselves: the algorithms, infinite scrolling and other engagement mechanisms that can repeatedly amplify harmful material, stir up negative emotions and incite troubling behaviours - all to bolster a business model built around attention, emotions, addition, data and advertising.

events.title: Brazil election: Lula vows to stand up to Trump
events.summary: Brazilian President Lula says he will confront President Donald Trump at the UN in New York, accusing him of interfering in Brazil's election as tensions between Washington and Brasília deepen. The dispute comes after US tariffs on Brazilian goods and Trump's support for Lula's rival, Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

events.title: Lebanon on Paris talks : 'the general sentiment here is very little hope'
events.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun is in Paris for talks with Emmanuel Macron, but on the ground many Lebanese say they have little hope after months of war with Israel, the continued occupation of parts of southern Lebanon and uncertainty over regional tensions. FRANCE 24's Renée David reports from Beirut on hopes that Aoun and Macron can rally international backing and secure a framework agreement to help stabilise the country.

events.title: From Then to Now: European Heritage Days and saving France's 'patrimoine'
events.summary: Whether it’s visiting a national monument, going behind-the-scenes at a television station or walking around a neighbour’s castle, millions participate every year in The European Heritage Days. We dive into how they got their start, why they're needed now more than ever, and how there's a new deal – the Patrimoine Pass – to support France's monuments.

events.title: US interest rate hike sparks Trump backlash
events.summary: The US Federal Reserve has raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, citing stubborn inflation despite pressure from President Donald Trump to cut borrowing costs. The decision prompted an immediate rebuke from Trump, while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh defended the central bank's independence and warned that inflation remains the priority.

events.title: Paris, the ultimate film set
events.summary: Paris has been a muse for filmmakers for over a century. The French capital has inspired countless scenes on the big screen. A new book brings them all together. Ruby Boukabou, author of 'The Movie Lovers' Guide to Paris', joins us to talk through her movie-themed walking tours in some of the city's most cinematic neighbourhoods.

events.title: DR Congo says Ebola outbreak has passed its peak
events.summary: More than 3,510 people have died from Ebola in eastern DR Congo since the outbreak was declared four months ago, with Ituri accounting for 78% of confirmed cases. Congolese authorities say the epidemic has now passed its peak, pointing to signs that the outbreak is beginning to slow.

events.title: Zimbabwe farmers brace for El Niño by saving water
events.summary: Some communities in Zimbabwe are adopting water-saving techniques such as aquaponics and rainwater harvesting to protect crops as the country braces for El Niño-driven drought. Sharon Mazingaizo has this report.

events.title: Tigray: 20,000 university students relocated by conflict
events.summary: Ethiopia's Education Ministry says around 20,000 university students in Tigray will be temporarily relocated to other public campuses after accusing the TPLF of using universities as military bases. The move comes as fighting and drone strikes continue in the northern region, with many students saying the trauma of the 2020-2022 Tigray war is still fresh. Our correspondent Tom Canetti reports from Addis Ababa.

events.title: Senegal farmers turn to fish and rice farming
events.summary: Some farmers in northern Senegal are combining fish farming with rice cultivation, using an age-old technique that helps fertilise fields, reduce pests and diversify incomes. The climate-smart approach is gaining renewed attention as communities adapt to growing environmental pressures.

events.title: Lebanon: UNIFIL withdrawal at the heart of Paris talks
events.summary: Emmanuel Macron welcomes Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Jordan's King Abdullah II to Paris today for talks on Lebanon's security and international support for the Lebanese army. The meeting comes as France pushes to prevent a security vacuum ahead of UNIFIL's planned withdrawal at the end of 2026, with Israeli strikes continuing in southern Lebanon and concerns growing over who will secure the border. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago has the latest.

events.title: Sweden: Andersson's centre left claims narrow win
events.summary: Sweden's centre-left opposition, led by Magdalena Andersson, is set to defeat the incumbent right-wing bloc by one seat after nearly all votes were counted in Sunday's election. The narrow result means coalition talks are likely to be challenging, with parliament due to begin the government formation process on September 28.

events.title: Erdogan to sidestep Turkey’s constitutional term limits in early 2028 vote, adviser says
events.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan intends to run in an early election in 2028 in order to circumvent the constitutional term limits he would face if he serves out his full current term, a top adviser said Thursday. Under Turkey's constitution, parliament can trigger early elections given the support of 360 lawmakers, meaning the ruling AKP and its nationalist ally MHP will need support of at least 34 more lawmakers.

events.title: Carney aims dig at Trump as he addresses EU
events.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has welcomed the chance to become an "associate member" of ‌the EU, while appearing to aim a dig at Donald Trump.

events.title: 'Reasonable grounds' US committed war crime in Iran school strike, UN experts claim

events.title: Deaths of nine women in South Africa could be 'linked to serial killer', police say

events.title: FA demands release of files on World Cup sell-off plan and Balogun red card row

events.title: Texas abortion ban caused pregnant woman’s death, lawsuit says
events.summary: The family of a Texas woman who died from a pregnancy-related complications is suing state Attorney General Ken Paxton and the hospital where she was treated, claiming the state’s ban on most abortions killed her.

events.title: Salvadorans with TPS don’t know how long their protections will last
events.summary: José Palma of the National TPS Alliance says wrong paperwork or advice can jeopardize future immigration status, as he argues immigrants here for 25 years should have a “permanent solution.”

events.title: Stocks and bonds rally after Fed hikes rates and oil prices fall
events.summary: U.S. stock indexes rose sharply Thursday after the Federal Reserve hiked interest rates in a bid to rein in rising inflation.

events.title: Singer Duncan Sheik in ‘critical but stable’ condition and receiving care
events.summary: Tony Award-winning singer and songwriter Duncan Sheik is in “critical but stable” condition and receiving medical care, according to a statement posted to his Instagram account Wednesday evening.

events.title: The portable power stations to use if your electricity goes out
events.summary: I spoke to experts to find the best power stations to charge phones, juice up small appliances during natural disasters and more.

events.title: Check your bathroom — you may have recalled hand soap sitting on your sink
events.summary: The FDA classified a recall of 2,696 cases of Intercon Chemical hand soap sold in 15 states after possible contamination with Pseudomonas and Serratia bacteria.

events.title: October Prime Day dates were just announced — here’s everything you need to know
events.summary: Prime Big Deal Days is Amazon’s second Prime Day-level sale of 2026 for loyalty members. These are the dates and details to know, plus what to expect.

events.title: Early October Prime Day deals just dropped — I found 31+ worth shopping
events.summary: Prime Big Deal Days starts on October 6, but early deals are already live. Shop products at least 20% off from Dyson, Garmin, Ninja and more.

events.title: What we know about the three lives lost in the NBCLA helicopter crash
events.summary: Eliana Moreno, an aerial photojournalist, and pilot George Marciniw died aboard the chopper. The third victim on the ground, Edy Gutiérrez Mejia, was visiting from Guatemala.

events.title: How Canada and the E.U. are teaming up to counter Trump
events.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg to lay out how middle powers might counteract Trump’s hostility.

events.title: Rubio takes behind-the-scenes role on Iran war, while keeping his options open for the future
events.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio isn’t the face of the Iran negotiations. He’s kept a discreet public distance as the unpopular war grinds on.

events.title: House passes Russia sanctions bill named for Lindsey Graham, sending it to Trump
events.summary: The legislation, which passed the Senate last month, would target Russia’s energy sector by punishing the largest buyers of its oil and gas to slash revenues Russia uses to attack Ukraine.

events.title: Saudi Arabia accuses Houthis of attacking Mecca, warns holy city is a ‘red line’
events.summary: The Iran-backed Yemeni rebels denied targeting the city in their escalating campaign against the key U.S. ally.

events.title: Canada poised to become European Union's first 'associate member'
events.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told the European Parliament in France that he is interested in making his country the first "associate member" of the E.U. It comes as Canada and western Europe's relationship with the U.S. has become strained in recent months. NBC News' Matt Bodner explains the benefits of the new alliance.

events.title: U.N. panel accuses U.S. of committing war crimes in Iran
events.summary: Human rights experts commissioned by the U.N.’s top human rights body say they have found “reasonable grounds” to believe the United States committed war crimes in two strikes in Iran, including on a school in the southern city of Minab. NBC News' Monica Alba reports on the accusations and potential consequences.

events.title: U.S. accuses Russia of plot to kill a prominent dissident in Washington
events.summary: The U.S. is accusing the Kremlin of orchestrating a murder-for-hire plot against a prominent Russian dissident in Washington, D.C., the Department of Justice has said. The five people who were charged are still at large. NBC News' Tom Winter has more on the charges.

events.title: Harry and Meghan change kids' school over security concerns
events.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, have transferred their children to another school shortly after they moved back to the U.K., over security concerns. The news comes as the couple await a verdict on their request for publicly-funded security protection.

events.title: King Charles issues fiery response to Princess Diana’s brother over claims in new book
events.summary: In a rare rebuke, Buckingham Palace issued a robust statement aimed at King Charles III’s former brother-in-law, Earl Charles Spencer, as he is set to release his bombshell memoir.

events.title: Australian athlete apologizes after winning race despite involuntary bowel movement
events.summary: An Australian athlete apologized Thursday for continuing — and winning — her race in China over the weekend after experiencing an involuntary bowel movement during competition.

events.title: New wild cat species is identified for first time in 100 years, researchers say
events.summary: Researchers say they’ve identified a new species of wild cat previously unknown to science. The Tilcayo tiger cat is smaller than a typical house cat and lives in the Bolivian cloud forest.

events.title: U.S. accuses Russia of plot to kill a prominent dissident in Washington
events.summary: The Justice Department unsealed charges against five people it alleged were part of the Kremlin’s “global assassination network” aimed at causing “destruction and mayhem.”

events.title: Hyrox co-founder apologizes after athlete allowed to continue despite defecating on herself
events.summary: Professional athlete Joanna Wietrzyk was seen on video and in photographs running and using shared fitness equipment with feces running down her legs.

events.title: U.S. and China face grave AI risks, but mutual distrust stalls cooperation
events.summary: Foremost among the threats for Beijing is the risk to the ruling Communist Party, which worries the technology could be weaponized against it.

events.title: Russia and Ukraine launch new attacks on energy despite Trump’s ceasefire claim
events.summary: The president’s statement that Moscow and Kyiv had agreed to pause strikes against each other’s energy infrastructure was followed by a night of strikes on energy infrastructure.

events.title: Harry and Meghan change their children’s school over security concerns
events.summary: Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, were enrolled in an undisclosed school when their parents moved back to Britain from California last month.

events.title: How Ukraine’s futuristic war could get ‘much worse,’ according to ex-Google CEO
events.summary: “The rate of innovation is faster than I’ve ever seen, and I work in tech,” Eric Schmidt told NBC News’ Richard Engel.

events.title: 10-year Treasury yield tops 5% as oil surges and diesel hits all-time high
events.summary: Talks between Iran and Gulf countries about the future of the Strait of Hormuz were delayed after a key Saudi pipeline was hit.

events.title: China dismisses AI slowdown calls and blasts ‘fearmongering’ from U.S. tech leaders
events.summary: Urgent calls for a slowdown in the development of artificial intelligence may cite a grave threat to humanity, but China says the warnings are instead aimed at slowing its progress as America’s rival superpower.

events.title: Saudi shutdown of key pipeline limits oil flow as Yemen hits back against Houthis
events.summary: Saudi Arabia has closed a critical oil pipeline after it was struck by drones launched from Iraq, with the latest squeeze reverberating through the region Saturday as attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels threatened to deepen the world’s energy crisis.

events.title: Strikes shut down key Saudi pipeline as Iran-backed Houthis tighten grip on crucial shipping lane
events.summary: Houthi rebels effectively completed a rapid push to take control of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline on Friday, tightening their grip on one of the world’s most important shipping routes and delivering a dramatic boost to their backers in Iran.

events.title: Emma Bonino, leader of abortion and divorce battles that changed Italy, dies at 78
events.summary: Emma Bonino, who rose to political prominence as a leader of campaigns by the Radical Party that legalized abortion and divorce in the 1970s in heavily Roman Catholic Italy, against the objections of the Vatican, has died.

events.title: They led vigils for victims of Tiananmen. Now they’re facing time in prison for it.
events.summary: Three pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong who organized annual vigils for victims of China’s 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown were sentenced Friday under a national security law that critics say has stifled dissent.
